title: Jesus our mother (ch. 58–60)
hook: Julian speaks of the motherhood of Christ, who feeds us with himself
tomorrow: why didn't God just stop sin before it ever started?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Julian's answer after years of asking: who showed it, what was shown, and why, all one word. The line was love was his meaning.

Sick on the couch, and someone keeps bringing soup you didn't ask for. They fix the blanket. They check your forehead. Part of you wants to say, I'm fine, I've got it. Julian of Norwich looks at exactly that kind of care, the feeding, the holding, the watching, and says Jesus does all of it, and more. She writes it calmly, without apology, as if it were plain. So why does she reach for the word mother?
screen: `SOUP YOU DIDN'T ASK FOR.` → `I'M FINE, I'VE GOT IT.` → `WHY THE WORD MOTHER?`

segments.voice: First, the claim. In chapter fifty-nine, Julian says that as truly as God is our Father, so truly God is our Mother. She doesn't drop the word Father. She sets Mother beside it, and she gives the mother's work in a special way to Christ, the second person of the Trinity. Second, the feeding. In chapter sixty she writes that a mother can give her child her milk, but our precious Mother Jesus can feed us with himself, and does, tenderly, in the Blessed Sacrament, which she calls the precious food of true life. For Catholics, that points straight to the Eucharist. Third, the holding. A mother can lay her child tenderly at her breast, she writes; Jesus can lead us into his own breast through his open side. Notice she still writes he. The motherhood is in what he does, not a change of name. Fourth, the root. The picture has one in the Gospel itself. In Matthew, Jesus says he longed to gather Jerusalem's children the way a hen gathers her chicks under her wings. So the answer to why mother: because feeding and holding are what she saw him do.
screen: `AS TRULY MOTHER AS FATHER.` · `HE FEEDS US WITH HIMSELF.` · `HELD AT HIS OPEN SIDE.` · `A HEN AND HER CHICKS.` · then, large: `MOTHER JESUS.`

segments.voice: Let your hands rest open in your lap, palms up, the way a small child's hands lie when someone else is doing the carrying. For the rest of the sit, don't fix or earn anything; let yourself be held, by the breath, by the quiet, and, if you pray, by God.
Jesus our mother. Julian's picture of Christ caring as a mother does: feeding us with himself, holding us close.
Carry this: mother Jesus, who feeds us with himself and doesn't mind the fuss. Rest well.

fork.setup: a friend's dad is home after surgery and turns down every offer of help: grown men don't get babied. what from Julian could you gently offer?
options: Julian says God is Mother instead of Father, so he should accept it.
Julian says suffering on your own is what makes you strong.
Julian pictures Christ himself feeding and holding us; being cared for isn't only for babies.
fork.reveal: Julian gives the mother's work of feeding and holding to Christ, and keeps the word Father too. receiving care is part of the picture, not a failure.

trapdoor: what you thought: a modern reworking of an old faith.
what it means: Julian's own image of Christ, who feeds and holds us as a mother does, with Father kept beside it.
what a scholar hears: chapters 58 to 60, where the second person of the Trinity is called our Mother, and the feeding is the Blessed Sacrament.
guess: Julian's picture of Christ caring for us as a mother
a title Catholics give Mary as the mother of Jesus
a hymn sung on Mother's Day in Julian's own parish
recall: Julian's answer: love, from the start

chat.says: burned my hand at work. abuela's on aloe and caldo duty. i hate being babied. tell her to stop?
options: Let her. Julian pictures being fed and held as how Christ cares for us. Receiving isn't weakness.
Tell her gently. Julian says real faith means growing past needing a mother's care at all.
Let her, but only since she's older. Being cared for is just something you put up with.
chat.meaning: Julian says Christ feeds and holds us as a mother does. Letting someone care for you is receiving, not failing.

Trinity.meaning: one God in three persons: Father, Son and Holy Spirit

Blessed Sacrament.meaning: a Catholic name for the Eucharist, Christ present in it

Eucharist.meaning: the sacrament of Christ's body and blood, received at Mass

Julian of Norwich.meaning: an English woman who wrote down the showings she received
